contentPolicy: All entries below are original illustrative FluentPath practice items. They are not copied from IELTS, Pearson PTE, or university exam papers. Review and document rights before adding any third-party material.

tasks.title: Writing · Task 2
tasks.instructions: Write an essay discussing the question and support your view with reasons and examples.
tasks.prompt: Some people believe cities should spend more money on public parks and community gardens. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
tasks.source: Original FluentPath practice item
tasks.rights: Created for this project; not official exam material

tasks.title: Reading · Urban green spaces
tasks.instructions: Read the passage, then answer all three questions.
tasks.passage: Urban green spaces can improve wellbeing by giving residents places to exercise and meet. Trees also reduce heat and absorb some air pollution. However, creating parks in crowded cities can be expensive, and their benefits depend on good maintenance.

questions.question: What is one environmental benefit of trees?
options: They make city parks less expensive.
They reduce heat and absorb some air pollution.
questions.explanation: The passage says trees reduce heat and absorb some air pollution.

questions.question: What can green spaces give residents a place to do?
options: Grow food for the whole city.
questions.explanation: The opening sentence says residents can use green spaces to exercise and meet.

questions.question: What do park benefits depend on?
questions.explanation: The passage says the benefits depend on good maintenance.

tasks.source: Original FluentPath practice passage and questions
tasks.rights: Created for this project; not official exam material

tasks.title: Listening · Garden workshop
tasks.instructions: Listen to the announcement, then answer all three questions.
tasks.audioScript: The student garden workshop will take place on Saturday, 18 May, from 10 a.m. to 1 p.m. Please meet at the east entrance. Bring gardening gloves if you have them; tools will be provided.

questions.question: On what date is the workshop?
questions.explanation: The announcement gives the date as Saturday, 18 May.

questions.question: Where should participants meet?
questions.explanation: Participants are asked to meet at the east entrance.

questions.question: What will be provided?
questions.explanation: Tools will be provided; gloves are optional to bring.

tasks.instructions: Write an essay presenting your position with reasons and examples.

tasks.title: Reading · Community libraries
tasks.instructions: Read the passage, then answer all three questions.
tasks.passage: Community libraries are changing alongside the needs of their users. Many now provide digital resources, language classes, quiet study areas and access to technology. While online information is widely available, libraries remain valuable because they offer reliable materials and welcoming spaces for people to learn together.

questions.question: Why does the passage say libraries remain valuable?
options: They offer reliable materials and welcoming places to learn.
They have replaced all online information.
questions.explanation: The passage identifies reliable materials and shared learning spaces as reasons libraries remain valuable.

questions.question: Which service is mentioned?
questions.explanation: The passage lists language classes among the services many libraries provide.

questions.question: How does the passage describe online information?
options: It can only be found in libraries.
questions.explanation: The passage says online information is widely available, while libraries still offer other value.

tasks.source: Original FluentPath practice passage and questions
tasks.rights: Created for this project; not official exam material

tasks.title: Listening · Urban trees
tasks.instructions: Listen to the short talk, then answer all three questions.
tasks.audioScript: Researchers studying urban trees found that tree cover can lower street temperatures during hot weather. The effect is strongest when trees form a connected canopy. The researchers note that planting alone is not enough; young trees need regular care and suitable locations to survive.

questions.question: What can tree cover do during hot weather?
questions.explanation: The speaker says tree cover can lower street temperatures during hot weather.

questions.question: When is the cooling effect strongest?
options: When trees form a connected canopy
questions.explanation: The effect is strongest when trees form a connected canopy.

questions.question: What do young trees need to survive?
questions.explanation: The speaker says young trees need regular care and suitable locations.

tasks.source: Original FluentPath listening script and questions
tasks.rights: Created for this project; not official exam material

tasks.title: Reading · Coastal wetlands
tasks.instructions: Read the passage, then answer all three questions.
tasks.passage: Coastal wetlands can reduce the force of some waves because their plants slow moving water and help hold sediment in place. They also provide habitat for birds and young fish. Restoration projects often begin by removing barriers to natural tidal movement. Researchers caution that restored wetlands cannot prevent every flood, and outcomes depend on local geography, water levels and long-term care.

questions.question: How can wetland plants help reduce wave force?
options: They slow water and hold sediment
They make the sea level fall
questions.explanation: The passage says plants slow moving water and help hold sediment in place.

questions.question: What is a common first step in restoration?
questions.explanation: Restoration often begins by removing barriers to natural tidal movement.

questions.question: What limitation do researchers mention?
questions.explanation: The passage explicitly says restored wetlands cannot prevent every flood.

tasks.source: Original FluentPath practice passage and questions
tasks.rights: Created for this project; not official exam material

tasks.title: Listening · Library changes
tasks.instructions: Listen to the announcement, then answer all three questions.
tasks.audioScript: The north campus library will extend its weekday opening hours from Monday, 3 June. It will now close at 9 p.m. instead of 7 p.m. The change follows a student survey, but the weekend schedule will stay the same for now. Group study rooms can be booked online up to seven days in advance. Please bring your student card to collect a room key.

questions.question: What is changing from 3 June?
questions.explanation: The library will close later on weekdays, at 9 p.m.

questions.question: Why were the new hours introduced?
questions.explanation: The announcement says the change follows a student survey.

questions.question: What should students bring to collect a room key?
questions.explanation: Students are asked to bring their student card.

tasks.title: Writing · Summarise a passage
tasks.instructions: Read the passage and write one sentence that captures its main idea and key supporting points.
tasks.prompt: Community energy projects allow residents to invest in local renewable power, such as solar panels on public buildings. Supporters say local ownership can keep some financial benefits in the area and help people understand how energy is produced. However, projects need clear management and enough initial funding. Their success also depends on suitable sites and continued maintenance, so they are not a complete solution for every neighbourhood.
tasks.source: Original FluentPath practice passage and prompt
tasks.rights: Created for this project; not official exam material

tasks.title: Reading · Sleep and learning
tasks.instructions: Read the passage, then answer all three questions.
tasks.passage: Sleep supports several processes involved in learning, including attention and memory. A short period of rest after studying may help some people organise what they have learned, but it cannot replace practice or make every learner perform equally well. Researchers also point out that sleep needs vary, and that study results from one group should not automatically be applied to everyone.

questions.question: Which learning processes are linked with sleep in the passage?
questions.explanation: The first sentence links sleep with attention and memory.

questions.question: What limitation is mentioned about rest after studying?
options: It removes the need for sleep
questions.explanation: The passage says rest cannot replace practice.

questions.question: Why should findings from one group be used carefully?
options: All studies use the same learners
questions.explanation: Researchers note that sleep needs vary and results may not apply to everyone.

tasks.source: Original FluentPath practice passage and questions
tasks.rights: Created for this project; not official exam material

tasks.title: Listening · Course registration
tasks.instructions: Listen to the announcement, then answer all three questions.
tasks.audioScript: Registration for the evening language course opens on Tuesday, 9 July. Classes begin the following week and meet on Tuesdays and Thursdays from 6 to 7:30 p.m. Students should complete the online form before attending. The first lesson is in Room 204, but later classes will move to the language centre. A printed workbook is included in the course fee.

questions.question: When does registration open?
questions.explanation: Registration opens on Tuesday, 9 July.

questions.question: How often do classes meet?
questions.explanation: The announcement gives Tuesday and Thursday as class days.

questions.question: What is included in the course fee?
questions.explanation: The workbook is included in the course fee.

tasks.title: Speaking · Retell a short lecture
tasks.instructions: Review the lecture notes, then summarise the main idea and two supporting details aloud.
tasks.prompt: Lecture notes: A university trial compared three ways to reduce food waste in student residences. Clearer date labels improved planning; smaller serving trays reduced leftovers; and a weekly donation collection redirected unopened food. The trial lasted eight weeks. The largest reduction came from combining all three changes, although the team recommends testing the approach in other settings.
tasks.source: Original FluentPath lecture notes and speaking prompt
tasks.rights: Created for this project; not official exam material

tasks.title: Writing · Compare recycling rates
tasks.instructions: Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make relevant comparisons.
tasks.prompt: A table shows the percentage of household waste recycled in three towns. In 2019, Northdale recycled 34%, Lakeside 28%, and Hillview 41%. In 2024, the figures were 46%, 39%, and 44% respectively. Write a report describing the main features and comparisons. Do not add reasons that are not shown by the data.

tasks.rights: Created for this project; not official exam material

tasks.instructions: Present your view and support it with clear reasons and relevant examples.
tasks.prompt: Some people believe governments should spend more money on museums and public galleries, while others think this money should be used for essential services. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.

tasks.title: Reading · Campus research spaces
tasks.instructions: Read the passage, then answer all three questions.
tasks.passage: A university converted an unused storage building into shared research rooms. The rooms can be booked by students from different departments, allowing them to borrow specialist equipment rather than buy it for a single project. A review after one year found that bookings rose during term time but fell sharply in summer. The university will keep the rooms open, while considering shorter summer hours. Staff also noted that shared equipment needs clear booking rules and regular maintenance.

questions.question: Why were the research rooms created?
options: To let students share specialist equipment
questions.explanation: Students can borrow specialist equipment instead of buying it for one project.

questions.question: When did bookings fall sharply?
options: At the start of each week
questions.explanation: The review found that bookings fell sharply in summer.

questions.question: What does shared equipment require?
options: A separate building for every student
questions.explanation: Staff said the equipment needs clear rules and regular maintenance.

tasks.source: Original FluentPath practice passage and questions
tasks.rights: Created for this project; not official exam material

tasks.title: Reading · Community seed banks
tasks.instructions: Read the passage, then answer all three questions.
tasks.passage: Community seed banks store locally collected seeds so that growers can use varieties suited to nearby conditions. Members may exchange seeds and record when and where each variety grows well. The banks do not guarantee a harvest: weather, soil and cultivation methods still matter. Organisers therefore combine seed storage with workshops and encourage members to keep some seeds from each successful crop for future seasons.

questions.question: Why do growers use locally collected seeds?
options: They remove the need to water plants
questions.explanation: The passage says the varieties may suit local conditions.

questions.question: What information do members record?
options: Where and when a variety grows well
The price of every garden tool
The number of workshops each year
questions.explanation: Members record when and where each variety grows well.

questions.question: Why are workshops included?
options: Seed storage alone cannot guarantee a harvest
Weather has no effect on crops
questions.explanation: The text says growing outcomes depend on more than stored seeds, so workshops support members.

tasks.source: Original FluentPath practice passage and questions
tasks.rights: Created for this project; not official exam material

tasks.title: Listening · Commuter survey
tasks.instructions: Listen to the briefing, then answer all three questions.
tasks.audioScript: The transport department surveyed 320 residents about their journeys to work. The largest group travelled by bus, while walking was the least common choice. Since the survey was conducted in October, the department plans to repeat it in spring to see whether the pattern changes. The results describe the people who replied; they should not be treated as a complete picture of every resident in the city.

questions.question: How many residents were surveyed?
questions.explanation: The speaker says 320 residents took part.

questions.question: Which travel choice was least common?
questions.explanation: Walking was the least common choice in the survey.

questions.question: Why will the department repeat the survey in spring?
options: To check whether the pattern changes
questions.explanation: The department wants to see whether the pattern changes by season.

tasks.source: Original FluentPath listening script and questions

tasks.audioScript: The geography field course will leave from the science building at 8:15 on Thursday morning. Students should bring a notebook, water and a light rain jacket. questions.explanation: The group will leave from the science building.

questions.question: What will the department provide?
questions.explanation: Safety equipment and lunch will be provided.

questions.question: When should students check for the final decision?
questions.explanation: Students should check their university email after 6 p.m. Wednesday.

tasks.title: Writing · Summarise urban farms
tasks.instructions: Read the passage and write one sentence that captures its main idea and key supporting points.
tasks.prompt: Urban farms use rooftops, courtyards and vacant lots to grow food close to consumers. Supporters say these projects can provide fresh produce and create opportunities for residents to learn about gardening. However, available space is limited, and farms need reliable access to water, suitable soil and ongoing volunteer or staff support. They are best understood as one part of a local food system rather than a replacement for larger farms.
tasks.source: Original FluentPath practice passage and prompt
tasks.rights: Created for this project; not official exam material

tasks.title: Reading · Bike-share patterns
tasks.instructions: Read the passage, then answer all three questions.
tasks.passage: A city compared bike-share journeys before and after opening a protected route beside the river. Use of nearby stations rose during the first six months, especially on weekdays. The report says this increase happened at the same time as the new route opened, but it does not prove the route was the only cause. Weather and changes in station locations may also have influenced the figures. The city plans to collect data for another year before deciding whether to extend the route.

questions.question: When did nearby station use rise?
options: During the first six months after the route opened
Before the city collected any data
questions.explanation: Use rose during the first six months after the route opened.

questions.question: What does the report say about the route and the increase?
options: The route is proven to be the only cause
The increase happened at the same time, but other factors may matter
The route reduced all bike-share use
questions.explanation: The report does not claim the route was the only cause.

questions.question: What will the city do before deciding about an extension?
questions.explanation: The city plans to collect data for another year.

tasks.source: Original FluentPath practice passage and questions
tasks.rights: Created for this project; not official exam material

tasks.title: Reading · Remote work study
tasks.instructions: Read the passage, then answer all three questions.
tasks.passage: A small company allowed one team to work remotely two days each week for three months. Most team members reported that they spent less time commuting, while some said it was harder to ask quick questions. The company found no clear change in the number of completed projects during the trial. Because the team was small and the trial was short, the manager said the results should guide a larger evaluation rather than settle the question for every workplace.

questions.question: What benefit did most team members report?
questions.explanation: Most team members reported spending less time commuting.

questions.question: What difficulty did some people mention?
questions.explanation: Some found it harder to ask quick questions.

questions.question: Why should the results be treated cautiously?
options: The team was small and the trial was short
questions.explanation: The manager cited the small team and short trial.

tasks.source: Original FluentPath practice passage and questions

tasks.title: Listening · Museum visit
tasks.instructions: Listen to the announcement, then answer all three questions.
tasks.audioScript: Welcome to the City Design Museum. We are open from 10 a.m. to 5 p.m. every day except Monday. The temporary exhibition on public spaces is on the second floor and is included with your entry ticket. A guided tour begins at 2 p.m. near the main staircase. Photography is permitted in the permanent galleries, but please do not take pictures in the temporary exhibition.

questions.question: On which day is the museum closed?
questions.explanation: The museum is open every day except Monday.

questions.question: Where is the temporary exhibition?
questions.explanation: The announcement places the exhibition on the second floor.

questions.question: Where may visitors take photographs?
questions.explanation: Photography is permitted in the permanent galleries only.

tasks.source: Original FluentPath listening script and questions
tasks.rights: Created for this project; not official exam material

tasks.title: Listening · Building energy use
tasks.instructions: Listen to the short talk, then answer all three questions.
tasks.audioScript: A campus team compared electricity use in two similar teaching buildings. One building used automated lighting controls, while the other relied on manual switches. Over the study period, the building with automated controls used less electricity for lighting, but the difference was smaller on cloudy days. The team recommends combining sensors with clear instructions so occupants can adjust settings when a room is unusually bright or busy.

questions.question: What did the team compare?
options: Electricity use in two teaching buildings
questions.explanation: The team compared electricity use in two similar teaching buildings.

questions.question: When was the difference in lighting use smaller?
questions.explanation: The speaker says the difference was smaller on cloudy days.

questions.question: What does the team recommend?
options: Sensors plus clear instructions for occupants
questions.explanation: The recommendation combines sensors with clear user instructions.
